title: The rule of law
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the rule of law, which is that everyone including government is bound by law and laws are known, fair and equally applied; the closest, Characteristics of an effective law, covers only whether a law is known, clear, stable, enforceable and reflects values.

draft.title: The rule of law
card: The rule of law means everyone must obey the law. This includes the government, police and public officials, not only ordinary citizens.
Laws must be known. They are made public, so people can find out what is allowed and what is not.
Laws must be fair and applied equally. Wealth, fame or power do not give anyone special treatment.
If a person or an official breaks the law, the same legal process applies to them as to anyone else. A court decides, not the person in power.
draft.remember: Nobody is above the law, and the same rules apply to all.

a.q: Which situation best shows the rule of law in action?
opts: A minister is charged and tried like any other person
A minister is excused because of the office they hold
A minister decides the penalty for their own offence
A minister can change a law to avoid being charged
a.why: The rule of law means government officials must obey the law and face the same legal process as everyone else. Excusing a minister because of their office is the tempting wrong answer, as it gives special treatment to someone with power.
a.clue: Does the person in power get special treatment?

b.q: Two drivers in Wagga Wagga are caught driving at the same speed in the same zone. One is a well-known local footballer. The court fines both the same amount. Why does this show the rule of law?
opts: The law was applied equally, whatever their fame
The law was kept secret until the court hearing
Only the footballer had to obey the speed limit
The court chose the fine based on who was popular
b.why: Both drivers faced the same law and the same penalty, so the law was applied equally. Fame gave the footballer no special treatment. The idea that fame might change the fine is the tempting mistake, and it is the opposite of the rule of law.
b.clue: Did being well known change what happened?

a.best: A minister is charged and tried like any other person

b.best: The law was applied equally, whatever their fame
